question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary when caring for a victim of breast ironing?

options.A: Hospitals require multiple signatures before prescribing simple painkillers
options.B: The patient needs medical, psychological, and social protection services
options.C: Physical wounds always heal faster when psychiatric drugs are given
options.D: Doctors are legally barred from treating burns without social workers

question: A patient with severe malaria is worried about losing income and how their family will eat while they are in the hospital. Which dimension of care is primarily affected here?

options.C: Social dimension
options.D: Spiritual dimension

question: Which of these patients has the highest risk of developing an obstetric fistula?

options.A: A young rural mother who laboured at home for three days without skilled help

options.C: A pregnant woman who attends all her routine antenatal care appointments
options.D: An older woman scheduled for an elective Caesarean section at a tertiary hospital

question: Which group of people has the highest risk of catching hydatid disease?

options.A: Shepherds and rural livestock farmers
options.B: Urban office workers and bankers
options.C: Desert nomads living without animals
options.D: Deep-sea fishermen and sailors

question: What is orthostatic hypotension?

options.A: A gradual increase in systolic pressure during physical exercise

options.C: An acute spike in blood pressure caused by emotional stress
options.D: A sudden drop in blood pressure when moving from sitting to standing

question: Where does spermatogenesis take place inside the testes?

options.A: Seminiferous tubules
options.B: Tunica albuginea

options.D: Bulbourethral glands

question: What is the golden rule for using syringes and needles in patient care?

options.A: They can be shared between family members in the same room

options.C: They can be reused if sterilized in boiling water first
options.D: They only need replacement if they appear bent or blunt

question: Back in the Middle Ages, who mainly cared for and sheltered the sick?

options.A: Religious orders and monasteries
options.B: Government ministries of health

options.D: Private health insurance companies

question: In public health, what does 'incidence' specifically measure?

question: What is a major social challenge faced by half-way houses in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive public demand for luxury hotel-style rooms

options.D: An overabundance of government funding and free resources

question: What does tumor 'staging' mainly tell the healthcare team?

options.A: The exact microscopic appearance and shape of the cells

options.C: The speed at which the patient's hair falls out
options.D: The specific type of chemotherapy needed for cure

explanation: Staging helps doctors figure out how big the tumor is and if it has traveled to other parts of the body. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the number one risk factor for developing a placenta accreta?

options.A: A history of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Previous uterine surgery or cesarean section
options.C: Eating a high-fat diet during pregnancy
options.D: Advanced maternal age over 40 years

question: What purpose does the cork bung serve when using a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It filters out dust particles before the patient breathes the vapor
options.B: It seals the top of the jar so steam escapes only through the mouthpiece
options.C: It measures the exact temperature of the water inside the container
options.D: It absorbs excess medication that spills during preparation

explanation: Well done! The cork acts as a tight lid, making sure all the warm steam is forced to travel upward through the central tube and out the mouthpiece where the patient needs it. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the main sterol found in the cell membrane of fungi?

options.A: Peptidoglycan
options.B: Cholesterol
options.C: Chitin
options.D: Ergosterol

explanation: Spot on! Fungal cell membranes use ergosterol. This is super helpful in pharmacology because many antifungal drugs target ergosterol, leaving our human cells (which use cholesterol) alone. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h1)

question: In the TSSU, what does the inventory rule 'FIFO' stand for?

options.A: Filtered-Instrument, Filtered-Object
options.B: Final-Item, Final-Order
options.C: Fast-Inspection, Fast-Operation
options.D: First-In, First-Out

explanation: Correct! FIFO means the supplies that arrived first get used first, keeping items from sitting on shelves past their expiration dates. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: What does 'food security' mean for a population?

options.A: Storing a ten-year supply of grains in underground bunkers
options.B: Having military protection around every food warehouse
options.C: Constant physical, social, and economic access to safe and enough food
options.D: Producing every single food item inside the country's borders

explanation: Food security simply means everyone has reliable access to enough safe, nutritious food to live a healthy life. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h2)

question: What happens to blood vessels when you apply a cold compress?

options.A: Vasoconstriction
options.B: Capillary rupture
options.C: Aneurysm formation
options.D: Vasodilation

explanation: Cold makes blood vessels narrow down (vasoconstriction), which slows down blood flow to the area and stops swelling from getting out of hand. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T9#GNS221_U3_T9_h2)

question: Once breastfeeding is well established (Lactogenesis III), how does the body keep making enough milk?

options.A: By continuous hormonal signals sent from the anterior pituitary gland
options.B: By the structural expansion of the lobulo-alveolar system
options.C: By high circulating levels of progesterone stored in adipose tissue
options.D: By an autocrine supply-and-demand mechanism based on milk removal

explanation: It's all about supply and demand! The more the baby feeds and empties the breast, the more milk your body gets the signal to make. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h4)

question: What is the main feature of a correlational study?

options.A: Variables are not manipulated by the researcher
options.B: Random assignment is used for all participants
options.C: A specific medication is tested on patients
options.D: Only laboratory animals are studied

explanation: Spot on! In correlational studies, we simply observe natural relationships without changing or controlling things ourselves. You've got this! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why do researchers use statistical tables alongside written text in a report?

options.A: Narrative text cannot contain numbers under any circumstance

options.C: Tables are meant to confuse readers who do not understand math
options.D: Tables are required by law for every medical document

explanation: Tables make heavy numbers easy to look at, which lets the written text focus on the most important patient care takeaways without getting cluttered. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to look at the whole picture—not just a single medical diagnosis—when caring for older adults?

options.A: Because doctors usually make mistakes when diagnosing elderly patients
options.B: Because patients only care about their emotional health
options.C: Because aging affects physical, mental, and social well-being simultaneously
options.D: Because chronic diseases disappear once the home environment is changed

explanation: You've got this! Older adults often face physical, emotional, and environmental challenges all at once. Looking at the big picture helps us give the best care possible. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a classic sign that a patient with diarrhoea is starting to get dehydrated?

options.A: Swelling in both lower legs and ankles
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor
options.C: Excessive production of clear saliva
options.D: Increased blood pressure and flushed skin

question: What is the solid ball of cells called that forms a few days after fertilization?

options.A: Trophoblast

options.D: Morula

question: Which parts of the spinal cord make up the sacral outflow of the parasympathetic nervous system?

options.C: S2 through S4
options.D: C1 through C5

question: What is the main feature of an urban 'food desert'?

options.A: Excessive government control over neighborhood food prices
options.B: A complete absence of any stores selling edible products
options.C: An abundance of local farms producing fresh vegetables
options.D: A lack of nearby supermarkets offering fresh, affordable food

question: Why is clear, objective nursing documentation so crucial in skilled care facilities?

options.C: It serves as a legal safeguard and proves that skilled criteria were met.

question: Why is picking the right research design so important for patient care?

options.A: It ensures findings can be trusted and safely applied to patients

options.C: It completely eliminates the possibility of human error
options.D: It reduces the time needed to collect patient data to zero

explanation: When we pick a solid research design, we get reliable evidence. That way, we can make safe, smart decisions right at the patient's bedside with confidence. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical audit in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To count the total number of visitors in the ward

options.D: To compare current nursing care against set standards

question: For how many months should an infant be exclusively breastfed (no other food or water)?

question: How should numbers inside a research table column normally be aligned?

question: What is the main goal of giving emergency contraception to a survivor of sexual assault?

question: When food prices shoot up way past family incomes, what do households usually do first?

question: What is the main physiological purpose of dietary proteins in the body?

question: Why does a cut or break in the skin raise a patient's risk of getting sick?

question: Which instrument is commonly used to gently grasp and pull out an implant rod during a removal procedure?

options.A: Large surgical scissors

options.D: Mosquito forceps

question: A newly widowed patient comes to the clinic looking very weak, dehydrated, and depressed after weeks of isolation. What should be the nurse's first step?

question: What is the main focus of 'internal validity' in a research study?

question: How does climate change directly throw a wrench into farming and crop production?

question: What is the core idea behind situational leadership in healthcare?

question: A patient has a kidney stone stuck right where the ureter crosses the major blood vessels near the pelvis. What is this spot called?

question: What exactly is a 'windshield survey' in community health nursing?

options.A: A formal written examination taken by student nurses before clinical rotation

question: As a community health nurse, what is your most important role in tackling the health effects of son preference?

question: What kind of data do you mainly collect in qualitative research?

question: At what age is primary amenorrhoea typically considered if a young girl has normal breast and pubic hair development but no period yet?

question: Why can a man still cause a pregnancy right after getting a vasectomy?

question: What is the main rule for deciding what counts toward a country's Gross National Product (GNP)?

question: Which of these habits will NOT help reduce overall inflammation in the body?

options.B: Managing chronic stress levels
options.C: Eating an anti-inflammatory diet
options.D: Smoking cigarettes daily

question: How does the complement system mainly attack invading bacteria?

question: Which of these is the most common and controllable risk factor for having a stroke?

question: Why do we tilt a pregnant woman in shock onto her left side during resuscitation?

question: What should you do right away if a patient says their eye pain and blurriness are getting worse during an irrigation?

question: Besides body movement, what is another vital function of skeletal muscle?

options.B: Filtering metabolic waste products from the blood

options.D: Generating body heat to maintain core temperature

question: Which of these is a complete 'no-go' (contraindication) when planning a home birth?

question: Which statement best demonstrates empathy toward a client struggling with a new diagnosis?

question: A public health team rushes to a village to investigate a sudden outbreak of measles only. What type of assessment are they doing?

question: When is a gastrostomy tube usually chosen over a nasogastric tube?

question: In history, why did many Nigerian communities use facial marks?

options.C: To treat severe bacterial infections
options.D: To prevent normal childhood growth

question: Where does a QA committee usually gather its data to check hospital performance?

question: What is the primary trigger for a cardiac action potential across cell membranes?

explanation: Effectiveness asks: does this treatment actually work for real patients outside of a laboratory test? [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h4)

question: How does a hormonal IUD locally affect the uterus to help prevent pregnancy?

options.A: It dilates the cervix to flush out incoming sperm
options.B: It stretches the muscle fibers to cause cramping
options.C: It secretes an enzyme that destroys ovarian follicles
options.D: It thins the endometrial lining significantly

explanation: The local release of progestin keeps the uterine lining nice and thin, making it impossible for a fertilized egg to plant itself. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T011#GNS226_U6_T011_h4)

question: According to the Nigerian immunization schedule, which vaccine is given to a newborn baby right at birth?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid booster
options.B: Yellow fever vaccine
options.C: Measles vaccine
options.D: BCG vaccine

explanation: Correct! BCG protects babies against tuberculosis and is given right away at birth alongside the polio drops. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why are elderly patients much more sensitive to side effects when taking multiple drugs?

options.A: They refuse to take any form of liquid medication or syrup.
options.B: Their immune systems reject synthetic chemical compounds instantly.
options.C: They always forget to take their medications at the correct hour.
options.D: Their bodies process and clear drugs more slowly due to aging organs.

explanation: As organs age, the liver and kidneys don't clear drugs as fast. This causes medications to hang around longer and build up in the body. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T9#GNS215_U1_T9_h3)

question: Under most Nigerian laws, what is the main legal exception that allows for an abortion?

options.A: If the family cannot afford a child
options.B: When requested by the husband
options.C: If the pregnancy occurs during school term
options.D: To save the life of the pregnant woman

explanation: Nigerian law is very strict regarding abortion, but saving the mother's life is recognized as a legal exception. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: What does nutritional literacy refer to?

options.A: The knowledge of traditional recipes from different cultures
options.B: The talent for cooking meals without using any salt
options.C: The ability to understand and use basic nutrition information
options.D: The skill of growing vegetables in small indoor spaces

explanation: Nutritional literacy is about comprehending food labels and dietary advice to make healthy choices for the body. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h4)

question: A client tells you she always forgets to take daily medications. What should your counseling approach be?

options.A: Insist that she must take combined oral pills exactly at dawn every day
options.B: Recommend a method that does not require daily action, like injectables
options.C: Suggest she set an alarm and force herself to use oral pills
options.D: Tell her that family planning is not suitable for her lifestyle

explanation: Good nursing meets the client where she is! Matching her actual lifestyle to a method she can easily manage prevents frustration. Well done! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why do public health campaigns often provide free childhood immunizations?

options.A: Pharmaceutical companies give away extra vaccines to charity for free
options.B: Vaccines create positive externalities by building community herd immunity
options.C: Infectious diseases never spread unless children are in school
options.D: Parents refuse to take their children to private clinics for shots

explanation: Brilliant! When you immunize a child, you don't just protect them—you shield the whole community by stopping the spread of disease. That's a powerful positive externality! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main idea behind person-centered care planning?

options.A: Allowing the nursing staff to make all daily decisions without input
options.B: Focusing solely on medical diagnoses while ignoring social history
options.C: Enforcing a strict morning schedule that all residents must follow
options.D: Tailoring care around the individual preferences and past routines of the resident

explanation: Exactly right! Person-centered care treats the resident as a unique human being, honoring their personal history and everyday preferences. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the key target recommended by the Abuja Declaration for national health budgets?

options.A: Less than 5% of annual tax revenue

options.C: Zero government spending on clinics
options.D: Exactly 50% of all foreign aid

question: When writing a research proposal for a study you haven't done yet, what tense should you use?

options.A: Future tense
options.B: Conditional tense
options.C: Present tense
options.D: Past tense

explanation: Since the research hasn't happened yet, you're planning for what you *will* do. That means keeping everything in the future tense! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is working hand-in-hand with traditional and religious leaders so helpful for contact tracing in local communities?

options.A: They personally conduct laboratory PCR testing for infectious diseases
options.B: They hold the trust of the people and help dispel harmful rumors
options.C: They are legally certified epidemiologists trained in data analysis
options.D: They provide the financial budget needed to buy hospital beds

explanation: Amazing! Local leaders are deeply trusted by community members, so when they support public health efforts, the community is much more willing to cooperate. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h7)

question: What is the main role of a community health nurse when dealing with child abuse?

options.A: Providing long-term foster care housing
options.B: Managing adult psychiatric disorders
options.C: Prosecuting offenders in a court of law
options.D: Population-level surveillance and early intervention

explanation: Spotting early warning signs in the community helps nurses catch issues before they turn into major traumas. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to keep checking updated clinical guidelines for managing reproductive health issues?

options.A: Outdated guidelines are always illegal to keep inside a nursing station
options.B: Medical protocols change as new research reveals safer ways to treat patients
options.C: Patients refuse care if nurses do not memorize every new research article
options.D: Hospital management requires proof of reading to approve annual salary increments

explanation: Medicine never stands still! Science constantly discovers safer ways to care for patients, so updating our knowledge helps us give the best care possible. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h4)

question: Who is typically a member of a Health Facility Development Committee?

options.A: Health workers and community representatives
options.B: International pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.C: Federal ministers of finance and education
options.D: State governors and local government chairmen

explanation: The HFDC brings together the people working inside the clinic and the community members using the services to ensure smooth daily operations. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the most reliable way to check if a patient actually has a nutrient deficiency?

options.A: Asking the patient what they ate yesterday
options.B: Observing the color of the patient's skin
options.C: Laboratory blood tests
options.D: Checking the patient's blood pressure

explanation: Lab tests give us clear, factual proof of what's inside the patient's blood, helping us avoid guessing or giving supplements they don't need. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h4)

question: What is a major health risk for a teenage athlete who consistently eats far fewer calories than their body burns?

options.A: Excessive increases in height growth
options.B: Instant muscle hypertrophy and strength gains
options.C: Delayed puberty and poor bone health
options.D: Improved long-term cardiovascular immunity

explanation: When growing teens don't get enough fuel, their hormone balance gets upset, which can delay puberty and weaken their bones. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h5)

question: How many weeks of pregnancy make up a normal term delivery?

options.A: Between 37 and 42 completed weeks
options.B: Between 28 and 34 completed weeks
options.C: Between 32 and 36 completed weeks
options.D: Exactly 40 completed weeks only

explanation: You've got this! A pregnancy is considered full term when it reaches anywhere from 37 up to 42 completed weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h1)

question: Why do we ask a patient to empty their bladder right before a proctoscopy?

options.A: To activate systemic blood pressure medications
options.B: To reduce pelvic pressure and enhance comfort
options.C: To prevent sudden urinary tract infections
options.D: To collect a routine clean-catch urine specimen

question: Which natural response generates heat through rapid, involuntary muscle movements?

options.A: Shivering
options.B: Vasoconstriction
options.C: Sweating
options.D: Vasodilation

question: Why is it important to document family planning care immediately after the encounter?

question: Which skin structure produces watery fluid to help cool the body through evaporation?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat cells

explanation: Great job! Eccrine sweat glands release water onto our skin, which cools us down as it evaporates into the air. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a well-known long-term health complication of Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhanced hormonal balance during adolescence
options.B: Permanent immunity to sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Obstructed labor and chronic pelvic infections
options.D: Complete elimination of menstrual cramps

explanation: FGM leaves behind scar tissue that can cause long-term pain and make childbirth terribly dangerous later in life. It's a key practice public health nurses actively campaign against. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T5#GNS225_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of instilling medication drops into the eye, ear, or nose?

options.A: To deliver slow-release nutrition directly into the blood
options.B: To completely flush out all natural body fluids
options.C: To provide direct local treatment to the affected area
options.D: To replace the need for all oral pain medications

explanation: Drops are applied straight to body cavities so the medicine works right where it is needed most. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which of these is actually helpful and NOT a barrier to hand hygiene on a busy ward?

options.A: Lack of skin moisturizers
options.B: Readily available sanitizer dispensers
options.C: Heavy patient workloads
options.D: Hand irritation and dermatitis

question: Which nursing action is strictly forbidden during the initial assessment of a patient bleeding in late pregnancy?

options.A: Checking the maternal blood pressure

options.D: Monitoring the fetal heart rate

question: What is the primary reason for keeping completed research questionnaires in a locked cabinet?

options.A: To ensure the forms do not get misplaced by staff

options.C: To protect patient confidentiality and privacy

question: A patient with unsteady balance and dizziness is admitted to the medical ward. What is the most immediate safety risk to prevent?

question: You check a mum on her 3rd day after birth. Where do you expect to feel her fundus?

options.B: About three fingerbreadths below the umbilicus

question: A patient cuts their forearm badly, damaging a major peripheral nerve, but months later sensation and movement return. What structure made this recovery possible?

options.A: Microglia replacing damaged muscle fibers
options.B: Oligodendrocytes wrapping the peripheral injury
options.C: Astrocytes migrating out of the spinal cord

question: What key information should you include in your verbal handover to the receiving nursing team?

options.D: The personal phone numbers of the transport crew

question: What is the best way for a nurse to prevent falls in a hospital ward?

options.A: Keeping all side rails locked in the fully raised position
options.B: Conducting individual risk assessments and targeted interventions
options.C: Removing call bells so patients do not attempt to get up alone
options.D: Restricting all patients to strict bed rest throughout their stay

question: Which personal protective equipment is essential when caring for a patient with airborne tuberculosis?

question: What distinct, tough patch does the diphtheria bacterium form in the throat?

question: If Florence Nightingale could whisper advice to you on the ward today, what would she say is the true focus of nursing?

options.C: Performing major surgical procedures

question: Which IPC measure is considered the single most effective action to prevent germ spread?

question: Which hormone has a sudden massive surge in the middle of the cycle to trigger ovulation?

question: A community nurse wants to reduce childhood vaccine drop-out rates in a rural district. Which PHC strategy is most appropriate?

question: Why must nurses be careful when giving cimetidine to patients taking many other drugs?

question: As a community health nurse, you notice many toddlers are malnourished in a farming village. Which non-medical sector should you involve first?

question: What is often the very first sign that a patient is bleeding after having their tonsils out?

question: What is a crucial check a nurse must do before giving any mucous membrane medication?

question: Which layer of the uterus is primarily responsible for contractions during childbirth?

question: Why is it important for a nurse to recognize the physical and psychological signs of early or forced marriage?

options.C: To automatically discharge the patient without further medical evaluation

question: What is the hierarchy of objectives in a healthcare organization?

question: Which heart rate pattern on a monitor is most commonly associated with uteroplacental insufficiency?

question: Which ethical principle is all about actively doing good and helping your patient?

question: Why must you record it carefully when a client decides to switch their contraceptive method?

question: Why are strong drugs like norepinephrine given through a central line instead of a regular vein in the hand or arm?

question: What happens during the coagulation and flocculation step of water treatment?

question: What is the primary goal of social services for persons with physical disabilities?

options.D: Replacing the need for medical rehabilitation

question: Why do community nurses take their analyzed data back to the community for validation?

question: What is the main purpose of an engineering control in the workplace?

question: Which type of inhaler needs a fast, forceful breath from the patient to work properly?

question: What does the Contraceptive Prevalence Rate (CPR) actually tell us?

options.C: The total number of children born in a single hospital per year

question: What is the main purpose of a bag-valve-mask (BVM) resuscitator?

question: Why is a formal approval process necessary before giving out free drugs from the DRF?

question: During a clinic health talk, you want to recommend affordable local Nigerian foods rich in iron. Which of these is best?

question: Which of the following best describes the multi-faceted role of a nurse working in a Nigerian primary health center?

question: Where should a urinary drainage bag always hang relative to the patient's bladder?

question: What is the medical term used when a patient's bad reaction stops after the suspected drug is withdrawn?

question: What is the main job of research objectives in a nursing study?

options.A: To prove the researcher's personal opinions
options.B: To replace the need for a literature review
options.C: To state what the study aims to achieve
options.D: To summarize the final conclusions of the study

explanation: Think of research objectives as your study's compass! They simply spell out what you intend to find out so your project stays on track. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h1)

question: A mother brings her healthy 14-week-old infant to the primary health clinic. Which group of vaccines is due for this visit?

options.A: BCG, OPV zero, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.B: Measles first dose and Yellow Fever vaccine
options.C: Rotavirus first dose and Pentavalent first dose
options.D: Pentavalent third dose, OPV 3, IPV, and PCV 3

explanation: At 14 weeks, infants receive the third doses of Pentavalent, OPV, and PCV, along with the first dose of Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of a true patient safety culture in a hospital?

options.A: Promoting collaborative teamwork across doctors and nurses
options.B: Finding root systemic causes when unexpected complications occur
options.C: Punishing individual staff members immediately for every minor mistake
options.D: Encouraging open discussion about accidental clinical errors

explanation: Blaming staff for minor errors creates fear, which stops people from reporting safety issues. A true safety culture focuses on learning! [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of giving a patient a naloxone kit upon discharge for opioid use?

options.A: To cure the underlying brain changes caused by long-term addiction
options.B: To reverse a potential life-threatening opioid overdose
options.C: To prevent the daily cravings for heroin or prescription pills
options.D: To serve as a daily vitamin replacement during recovery

explanation: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist that rapidly blocks opioid receptors, restoring normal breathing during an accidental overdose. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which action is strictly forbidden when handling used injection needles to prevent injuries?

options.A: Recapping needles by hand
options.B: Placing needles in a puncture-resistant bin
options.C: Reporting a sharps stick immediately
options.D: Carrying a tray with a used syringe

explanation: Correct! Never recap needles by hand—it's a leading cause of accidental needlestick injuries in the clinic. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h4)

question: What is the name of the specific space that directly surrounds and protects the human heart?

options.A: cranial cavity
options.B: pleural cavity
options.C: pericardial cavity
options.D: mediastinum cavity

explanation: Think 'peri' for around and 'cardio' for heart! The pericardial cavity is the cozy, fluid-filled space right around your heart. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which nervous system kicks in when a patient practices slow, deep breathing?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Somatic nervous system
options.C: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.D: Sympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing signals your vagus nerve to turn on the parasympathetic system—your body's wonderful 'rest-and-digest' mode that cools everything down. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h7)

question: Which drink should you avoid giving a child right after a tonsillectomy?

options.A: Vanilla ice cream
options.B: Clear apple juice
options.C: Red-colored juice
options.D: Plain cold water

explanation: You got it! Stay away from red drinks because if the patient throws up, the red color looks just like fresh blood and causes unnecessary panic. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h5)

question: When do Lassa fever outbreaks usually peak in Nigeria?

options.A: November to May
options.B: Throughout the entire year equally
options.C: September to October
options.D: June to August

explanation: You'll see more cases during the dry season. Bush burning and farming drive rodents closer to human homes looking for food and shelter. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h1)

question: A nurse is removing an IV line from a patient taking daily blood-thinning medication. What action is most important?

options.A: Skip the sterile gauze pad and apply transparent tape right away
options.B: Remove the cannula at a steep 45-degree angle to seal the skin
options.C: Apply firm, prolonged pressure to the site until bleeding stops completely
options.D: Massage the puncture site vigorously to stimulate local circulation

explanation: Patients on blood thinners bleed longer, so extended direct pressure prevents large hematomas from forming. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h9)

question: Why do human-made disasters often catch us off guard and create complex challenges?

options.A: They only affect critical infrastructure and leave human populations unharmed
options.B: They strike suddenly without warning and leave behind persistent secondary dangers
options.C: They are easily contained and never require outside medical assistance
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of subsequent environmental contamination

explanation: Great thinking! Because these events happen without warning and leave behind things like toxic smoke or weak buildings, they keep emergency responders on high alert. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is a very common emotional experience for patients facing the end of their lives?

options.A: Existential distress and questioning life meaning
options.B: An intense desire to run marathons
options.C: Complete indifference to surroundings and people
options.D: Sudden loss of all emotional feelings

explanation: You got it! Toward the end of life, it's completely normal for patients to look back, wonder about their life's purpose, and work through big deep questions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h5)

question: What does it mean to write a 'contemporaneous' nursing note?

options.A: It is written using official medical shorthand
options.B: It is written at the end of the entire work week
options.C: It is written close to the time care is given
options.D: It is written by a senior doctor only

explanation: Spot on! Writing notes right away means you don't have to rely on memory, keeping the true timeline safe. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which chemical element is found in proteins (amino acids) but is generally absent in pure carbs and fats?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Nitrogen
options.C: Phosphorus
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Spot on! Every amino acid contains a special amine group made of nitrogen, setting proteins apart from carbs and fats. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h4)

question: What does a Timed Up and Go (TUG) test primarily evaluate?

options.A: Mobility, balance, and fall risk
options.B: Lung capacity and breathing rate
options.C: Cardiovascular endurance during rest
options.D: Upper body strength and grip

explanation: The TUG test observes a patient rising from a chair, walking a short distance, and returning, which directly measures functional mobility and balance. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h2)

question: Why do our hands and fingers take up such a huge chunk of space on the motor homunculus?

options.A: They require intricate, precise, and complex motor control
options.B: They have a much larger physical mass than the legs
options.C: They are closer to the brain than the lower extremities
options.D: They contain more bone density than other body parts

explanation: Makes total sense when you think about it—parts of the body that do delicate, skilled work (like typing or writing) get more brain real estate! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h3)

question: How does community stigma negatively affect disease surveillance efforts?

options.A: It encourages patients to report early to tertiary medical centers
options.B: It improves the accuracy of hospital laboratory diagnostic registers
options.C: It forces public health officers to increase local vaccination budgets
options.D: It causes families to hide sick members, leading to missed cases and deaths

explanation: Spot on! When people are afraid of being stigmatized, they hide their sick loved ones, making it tough for health workers to track and stop outbreaks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h8)

question: If a ward suddenly sees many more surgical site infections because of a poorly sterilized batch of tools, what kind of variation is this?

options.A: Special cause variation
options.B: Common cause variation
options.C: Standard baseline variation
options.D: Theoretical variation

explanation: This is a special cause variation because it is an unexpected, unusual event caused by a specific problem that needs fixing right away. [learn more](GST319_U2_T7#GST319_U2_T7_h4)

question: What happens if a patient uses over-the-counter medicated nasal sprays for too many days in a row?

options.A: Rebound nasal congestion
options.B: Severe fungal ear infections
options.C: Systemic high blood pressure
options.D: Permanent loss of the sense of smell

explanation: Exactly! Overusing these sprays causes the blood vessels in the nose to swell right back up even worse once the drug wears off. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h4)

question: What should a nursing unit manager do immediately after setting targets with the staff?

options.A: Punish nurses who ask questions about the goals
options.B: File the document away until the end of the year
options.C: Hand over all leadership duties to junior staff
options.D: Support staff in carrying out daily duties toward those targets

explanation: After goals are set, the actual work phase begins where staff execute plans and management provides support. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which type of seizure starts in only one specific area of the brain?

options.A: Focal seizure
options.B: Generalized seizure
options.C: Tonic-clonic seizure
options.D: Absence seizure

explanation: Focal seizures originate in a localized region of the brain, affecting only part of the body or awareness. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h3)

question: A choking patient suddenly passes out and falls to the floor. What should you do right away?

options.A: Start chest compressions and check the mouth for the object
options.B: Prepare to perform a surgical opening in the neck
options.C: Give an emergency injection of adrenaline
options.D: Prop the patient up in a high sitting position in bed

explanation: Once a choking victim collapses, you transition into CPR. Pumping the chest helps push air against the blockage, and you can check the mouth to scoop out the object if you see it. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h6)

question: How does poor quality care directly impact women seeking reproductive health services?

options.A: It encourages them to report staff members to management
options.B: It forces them to demand more expensive medications
options.C: It drives them toward unsafe, alternative healthcare sources
options.D: It has no measurable effect on their health-seeking habits

explanation: Unwelcoming environments, rudeness, and poor treatment discourage clients from visiting formal facilities, pushing them to seek help elsewhere. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h1)

question: What happens if hazardous waste accidentally gets thrown into the same bin as ordinary office paper?

options.A: The local municipal workers will sort it out safely at the dump
options.B: The total volume of waste instantly decreases by half
options.C: The entire combined batch must be treated as hazardous waste
options.D: The office paper automatically sterilizes the hazardous waste

explanation: Once clean and hazardous waste mix, you can no longer separate them safely. The whole bag now has to be treated as hazardous waste, which costs more and increases risk! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h2)

question: Which part of the spinal cord controls the parasympathetic signals needed for an erection?

options.A: T1 to T4
options.B: L1 to L3
options.C: S2 to S4
options.D: C1 to C3

explanation: Awesome! The sacral region (S2 to S4) is the powerhouse for sending parasympathetic signals down to trigger an erection. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T4#GNS121_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard reason for routine lab testing in dairy production?

options.A: Checking for excessive bacterial load in raw milk supplies
options.B: Guaranteeing that the milk contains zero water molecules
options.C: Confirming the success of the pasteurization process
options.D: Verifying the overall sanitation of milking equipment

explanation: Spot on! Microbiological tests look for bacteria and check if pasteurization worked. Water content is measured separately using physics methods like cryoscopy, not germ tests! [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h6)

question: How do quality improvement teams use data like fall rates and skin injury reports?

options.A: To hide negative clinical outcomes from state regulatory agencies.
options.B: To track performance trends and guide system-wide safety improvements.
options.C: To find individual nurses to blame whenever an accident happens.
options.D: To determine which residents should be discharged immediately.

explanation: Quality improvement isn't about blaming people—it's about spotting trends so we can make our hospital or facility safer for everyone! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h8)

question: What instructions should a nurse give a patient regarding care of the Mantoux injection site?

options.A: Massage ointment into the skin to reduce swelling
options.B: Keep the area clean, dry, and uncovered without scratching
options.C: Apply a medicated adhesive bandage over the bleb immediately
options.D: Wash the site vigorously with hot soapy water twice a day

explanation: Patients should leave the site alone, avoiding scratching or covering it, to ensure the local skin reaction remains undisturbed until it is read. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h8)

question: A massive movement of young people from rural farming villages into a crowded capital city is an example of which demographic process?

options.A: High fertility
options.B: Child mortality
options.C: Population capping
options.D: Internal migration

explanation: When people move from one place to another within the same country—like leaving the village for the city—we call it internal migration. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h3)

question: Where is the best place inside a refrigerator to store raw chicken breasts?

options.A: Inside the door racks
options.B: On the lowest shelf
options.C: On the top shelf
options.D: Next to fresh lettuce

explanation: Placing raw meat on the bottom shelf prevents blood and juices from dripping onto other foods that will not be cooked further. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h4)

question: Why does a comprehensive assessment in day care include evaluating the family caregiver?

options.A: To legally transfer family financial assets to the facility
options.B: To determine if the caregiver has a valid nursing license
options.C: To replace family involvement entirely with facility staff
options.D: To gauge caregiver stress and the sustainability of home care

explanation: Understanding caregiver strain helps the nursing team provide proper support and respite services, ensuring the client can safely remain at home. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h4)

question: Which action best shows you are advocating for your patient at the end of life?

options.A: Withholding pain medication to keep the patient awake for visiting relatives
options.B: Ignoring advance directives if the attending physician disagrees with them
options.C: Ensuring a documented DNR order is followed despite objections from distant relatives
options.D: Following the loudest family member's demand to start aggressive CPR

explanation: As a nurse, your duty is to protect the patient's documented wishes, even when family members disagree. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h5)

question: A patient comes to the clinic struggling with a weak urine stream after a past pelvic injury. What procedure are they most likely getting ready for?

options.A: Gastric tube insertion
options.B: Urethral dilation
options.C: Endotracheal intubation
options.D: Esophageal manometry

explanation: Pelvic trauma can cause scarring in the urethra (the urine passage), leading to a tight spot or stricture that needs to be gently stretched out to restore normal flow. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the main goal when treating a patient who has amenorrhoea?

options.A: Surgically removing the ovaries to stop hormone swings
options.B: Immediately restoring natural fertility in every case
options.C: Treating the specific underlying root cause
options.D: Preventing future pregnancy with strong contraceptives

explanation: Because amenorrhoea is a sign of something else, our treatment focuses on fixing the root problem—whether it is lifestyle, hormones, or anatomy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h6)

question: What primary role does the family unit play in the food supply chain?

options.A: It acts as the final link that consumes and utilizes the food.
options.B: It regulates international trade agreements for agricultural goods.
options.C: It determines large-scale industrial farming methods.
options.D: It sets global market prices for staple crops.

explanation: Families sit at the end of the supply chain, turning raw food into meals and nutrition for household members. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h1)

question: Which factor contributes heavily to nursing staff shortages in many Nigerian health units?

options.A: Mandatory retirement at age twenty-five
options.B: The migration of experienced nurses abroad
options.C: Strict laws banning hospital employment
options.D: A complete lack of nursing training schools

explanation: You're spot on. The 'japa' wave has caused many skilled nurses to move abroad for better opportunities, leaving local units short-staffed. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h8)

question: Where can you usually find the meanings of abbreviations or symbols used inside a table?

options.A: On the title page of the research paper
options.B: In the footnotes directly below the table
options.C: In the middle of the table body
options.D: In the reference list at the very end

explanation: Footnotes sit right underneath the table to explain any short forms or symbols, so you don't have to stress searching through the whole paper. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is a common tobacco trend among young people in Nigerian cities today?

options.A: A total shift toward chewing raw tobacco leaves exclusively
options.B: A complete halt in all forms of smoking
options.C: The rising popularity of manufactured cigarettes and shisha
options.D: The replacement of tobacco with herbal medicinal teas

explanation: Smart marketing has made manufactured cigarettes and waterpipes (shisha) very popular among urban youth. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to getting disaster information out to the public?

options.A: Excessive availability of accurate and simple translations
options.B: Cultural mistrust of government institutions
options.C: Language differences among different population groups
options.D: Physical disabilities that limit access to alerts

explanation: Correct! Having easy-to-read translations actually helps communication. It's the *lack* of them that creates a barrier. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why is family planning counseling a key part of post-abortion care?

options.A: To ensure the client conceives again within the next month
options.B: To fulfill a hospital administrative requirement unrelated to health
options.C: To help the client prevent future unintended pregnancies and repeat procedures
options.D: To punish the client for experiencing a pregnancy loss

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps clients protect their health and avoid another unplanned pregnancy down the line. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Which of these commonly stops Nigerian women from using contraceptives?

options.A: Mandatory counseling sessions required weekly
options.B: Laws that punish women for having children
options.C: Fear of side effects and partner disapproval
options.D: An excess supply of free medications in local markets

explanation: Myths about side effects and lack of support from partners or family members are major hurdles. Gentle, accurate counseling from nurses helps clear up these fears! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main job of the insufflation system during a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: To deliver numbing medicine to the colon
options.B: To cool down the light inside the scope
options.C: To suck out liquid stool and blood
options.D: To gently inflate the bowel with air or gas so the doctor can see better

explanation: You got it! Puffing a little air into the bowel opens up the folds of tissue so the doctor gets a clear view. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which muscle does most of the heavy lifting when you take a normal, quiet breath in?

options.A: Internal intercostals
options.B: Sternocleidomastoid
options.C: Rectus abdominis
options.D: Diaphragm

explanation: Correct! The dome-shaped diaphragm is your main breathing muscle, moving down to pull air into your chest effortlessly. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient on a bedpan is struggling to urinate while lying flat. What should you try first?

options.A: Assist the patient into a more natural, upright sitting position
options.B: Restrict all fluid intake for the rest of the day
options.C: Insert an indwelling catheter immediately without further delay
options.D: Administer a strong diuretic medication by mouth

explanation: Gravity and a normal sitting posture help relax the muscles, making it much easier to pass urine naturally. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h4)

question: In safety management, what is considered the MOST effective way to deal with a hazard?

options.A: Using administrative policies
options.B: Conducting safety training
options.C: Elimination of the hazard
options.D: Wearing protective gloves

explanation: If you completely remove the danger, nobody can get hurt by it! That makes elimination the ultimate win in safety. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a smart move when a mother suddenly starts bleeding heavily postpartum (PPH)?

options.A: Calling for immediate help from the obstetric and anesthesia team
options.B: Telling the patient to walk around the room to encourage blood flow
options.C: Massaging the uterine fundus to encourage muscular contraction
options.D: Starting large-bore intravenous lines for fluid and blood replacement

explanation: Never let a bleeding mum walk around! That can cause her blood pressure to crash and lead to shock. Keep her resting safely in bed while you call for backup. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h6)

question: Why is it correct to say gender roles are social constructs?

options.A: Because they are identical in every country across the world
options.B: Because they depend strictly on the presence of the Y chromosome
options.C: Because they are permanently encoded in human DNA at conception
options.D: Because they are created by human cultures and change across different times and places

explanation: Well done! Because they are human-made rules, gender roles change from culture to culture and shift over time. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h5)

question: As a nurse explaining a treatment plan, what should you avoid doing?

options.A: Using heavy medical jargon that the patient does not understand
options.B: Ensuring the conversation remains strictly confidential
options.C: Explaining the importance of abstaining from sex during treatment
options.D: Asking the patient about her current sexual partners

explanation: Always keep it simple! Heavy medical grammar just confuses patients. Talk to them in clear, everyday language they can easily grasp. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the main goal of doing a nutritional check on a patient in primary health care?

options.A: To evaluate nutritional status and spot early signs of health issues
options.B: To calculate the exact household income of a patient
options.C: To prescribe expensive vitamin supplements for every patient
options.D: To diagnose rare genetic disorders affecting body weight

explanation: Spotting poor nutrition early helps you step in with advice before the patient gets seriously ill. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T19#GNS214_U1_T19_h1)

question: Which two major veins join together to form the hepatic portal vein?

options.A: Superior mesenteric vein and splenic vein
options.B: Hepatic vein and inferior mesenteric vein
options.C: Internal jugular vein and subclavian vein
options.D: Inferior vena cava and renal vein

explanation: You'll find this intersection right behind the pancreas! The superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein team up to form the hepatic portal vein carrying blood right to the liver. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when designing a pie chart?

options.A: Grouping very small categories into an 'Other' slice
options.B: Including ten or more distinct slices for detail
options.C: Keeping the total sum strictly at 100 percent
options.D: Labeling percentages directly on the slices

explanation: You nailed it! Cramming ten or more slices into one pie creates a messy chart that nobody can read easily. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T8#GNS217_U4_T8_h6)

question: A patient develops a fungal mouth infection (oral thrush) after taking strong antibiotics. Why did this happen?

options.A: Antibiotics caused the patient's immune system to stop producing white blood cells
options.B: The medication directly stimulated the rapid growth of fungal spores in the throat
options.C: The antibiotics destroyed the protective normal bacteria that usually keep the fungus in check
options.D: The patient consumed contaminated food while taking the prescribed pills

explanation: Strong antibiotics are like a bomb in the gut and mouth—they wipe out the good bacteria that normally keep fungi like Candida under control, letting the fungus multiply unchecked. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is teamwork between a dietitian and a pharmacist so important for patient safety?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital meal trays
options.B: To determine when the patient is ready for hospital discharge
options.C: To decide which nurse will feed the patient during the shift
options.D: To prevent bad interactions between food and prescribed drugs

explanation: Certain foods can block or dangerously increase how medications work, making a joint review by dietitians and pharmacists super important. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T001#GNS227_U4_T001_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: Conducting laboratory research on new medications
options.B: Treating individual patients in hospital wards
options.C: Tracking health data to guide planning and action
options.D: Managing hospital financial budgets and staff

explanation: Surveillance focuses on collecting and analyzing population health data so authorities can take proper action to protect the public. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: What is your very first step when a patient has dry chemical powder spilled all over their skin?

options.A: Wrap the area tightly with a clean sterile bandage
options.B: Scrub the affected skin vigorously with a stiff brush
options.C: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly over the powder
options.D: Brush away the loose powder before using water

explanation: Always brush dry powder off first! Adding water right away to some chemicals can trigger a fiery reaction or make the chemical burn worse. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T5#GNS215_U5_T5_h4)

question: How does being severely underweight most often lead to fertility challenges in women?

options.A: By destroying existing ovarian follicles immediately
options.B: By halting ovulation through hypothalamic suppression
options.C: By causing physical blockage of the fallopian tubes
options.D: By thickening the cervical mucus permanently

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Extremely low body fat confuses the brain's hormone signals, which pauses the menstrual cycle and stops the release of eggs. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: What does a very large volume of distribution tell us about a drug?

options.A: The kidneys are getting rid of the drug too fast
options.B: The patient's liver is breaking down the medicine rapidly
options.C: The drug has moved heavily out of the blood and into body tissues
options.D: The drug is trapped strictly inside the blood vessels

explanation: A high volume of distribution means the drug loves hiding out in fat or muscle and leaves very little of itself floating behind in the blood. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h5)

question: A child with cerebral palsy presents with very stiff muscles and hyperactive reflexes. Which type of cerebral palsy is this child most likely experiencing?

options.A: Ataxic
options.B: Dyskinetic
options.C: Flaccid
options.D: Spastic

explanation: Spastic cerebral palsy is marked by increased muscle tone and exaggerated reflexes because of injury to the motor cortex or pyramidal tracts. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h3)

question: How would you best describe a skin macule?

options.A: A solid, elevated lump deep in the skin
options.B: A fluid-filled blister larger than one centimeter
options.C: A flat, unraised change in skin color
options.D: A raised, hard plateau made of merged bumps

explanation: A macule is completely flat. You can't feel it by running your finger over it—it's simply a change in color, like a freckle. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which sign is commonly seen in school-aged children with an undiagnosed learning disability?

options.A: Total loss of voluntary motor movement
options.B: Complete inability to recognize family members
options.C: Sudden blindness occurring only at night
options.D: Persistent reading errors and letter reversals

explanation: School-aged children typically show signs through ongoing struggles with reading, spelling, and academic tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is one major limitation of case-control studies?

options.A: They cost more money than clinical trials
options.B: They cannot include human subjects
options.C: They take many decades to complete
options.D: They are susceptible to recall bias

explanation: You got it! Because we rely on people remembering the past, honest memory gaps can lead to recall bias. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h6)

question: What do we call the fraction of a drug that successfully reaches the bloodstream in an active, unchanged form?

options.A: Clearance rate
options.B: Half-life
options.C: Bioavailability
options.D: Volume of distribution

explanation: Bioavailability simply means 'how much active drug is actually available' to your body to do its job after the journey. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h6)

question: A pregnant woman with obstructed labor is kept at a primary health clinic for three days trying local herbs before referral. Which principle of referral was violated?

options.A: Patient confidentiality
options.B: Financial auditing
options.C: Medication dispensing
options.D: Timeliness

explanation: Delayed transfer in an emergency violates the principle of timeliness, putting the mother and baby at severe risk. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h3)

question: A male patient comes in complaining of a thick, pus-like discharge from his private part. Which infection is the most likely suspect?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Gonorrhoea
options.C: Primary syphilis
options.D: Genital herpes

explanation: Spot on! Gonorrhoea in men is classic for that heavy, purulent (pus-like) urethral discharge and burning when peeing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which hygiene habit should nurses advise patients to ditch because it washes away protective vaginal flora?

options.A: Wiping front to back
options.B: Douching
options.C: Wearing cotton underwear
options.D: Washing with plain water

explanation: Douching disrupts that natural acidic balance and flushes out our helpful lactobacilli friends, opening the door wide for infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is widely recognized as the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Using disposable plates
options.C: Isolating every patient
options.D: Proper hand hygiene

explanation: Simple, thorough handwashing is your number one superpower as a nurse for keeping hospital germs away from vulnerable patients! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h6)

question: How does the stress-relaxation response help an organ like your urinary bladder?

options.A: It forces the organ to empty immediately when it reaches half capacity
options.B: It prevents the muscle cells from ever fatiguing during hard work
options.C: It generates rapid pumping movements to mix internal contents
options.D: It allows the organ to stretch to hold more fluid without a sharp pressure spike

explanation: This clever response lets your bladder gradually accommodate more fluid as it fills up, preventing sudden uncomfortable pressure spikes. Nursing clinicals will make this super clear too! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why is it important for a nurse educator to know and use more than one teaching method?

options.A: Hospital management mandates a change of method every single week
options.B: Different learning objectives and situations require different instructional approaches
options.C: Using multiple methods is the only way to assign passing grades
options.D: Students lose their nursing license if they experience only one teaching style

explanation: Just like you wouldn't use the same nursing procedure for every patient, you can't teach anatomy theory the exact same way you teach emergency resuscitation skills. Variety helps concepts stick! [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h1)

question: Why is accurate nutritional documentation important among members of the healthcare team?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers entirely
options.B: It prevents the hospital from having to buy specialized nutritional supplements
options.C: It ensures clear communication between nurses, doctors, and dietitians for coordinated care
options.D: It is only used for insurance billing and has no role in clinical treatment

explanation: Clear notes allow every healthcare provider involved in the patient's care to understand their nutritional status and treatment plan. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h7)
